name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Gate auto-apply on a semantic diff test that runs only against edited files. This keeps the system safe by verifying changes don’t break existing behavior while avoiding the cost of full-project regression checks. The trade-off is that edits might still introduce bugs in untested parts of the codebase, but that risk is lower than the overhead of running full tests on every change.

name: Gauge
text: The semantic diff test only catches changes that break *tested* behavior—it won’t flag edits that subtly alter untested logic or introduce new bugs in untouched files. A better alternative is to run a *targeted* regression suite on the edited files’ dependencies, not just the files themselves. Settle it by proving the regression suite catches the edge cases the semantic diff misses.
